AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 1, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-15-21, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE
FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING
THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709
573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER
CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  RICK RAMIREZ, MAYOR
  ANA VALENCIA, VICE MAYOR
  TONY AYALA, COUNCILMEMBER
  JENNIFER PEREZ, COUNCILMEMBER
  MARGARITA L. RIOS, COUNCILMEMBER
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING - 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION
  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(4) in one case.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Daniel Jansson
  Imago Dei Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Ximena Castillo, 5th grade
  Paddison Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to proclaim the month of February 2022 as National African American History Month in the
  City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to proclaim February 7-11, 2022 as National School Counseling Week in the City of
  Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Sheriff Alex Villanueva Regarding Moratorium on Contract Enhancements.

  3.  Recognition of Diego Pineda, Public Safety Sergeant and Mark Ortiz and George Valdez, Maintenance
  Workers IIIs, Homeless Operation Prevention Engagement Team.

  4.  Recognition of Los Angeles County Deputy Steven Douma upon his retirement.

  5.  Video highlighting Public Safety.
   6.  Week in Review video.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  January 18, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period December 26, 2021 –
  January 8, 2022, in the total amount of $944,011.63. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  January 13, 2022 – January 26, 2022, in the total amount of $2,440,735.11. 640

  Report

  5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Vanessa
  Williams. 830-23

  Report

  6.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – JANUARY 26, 2022 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  7.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-09 – DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – CITY CLERK
  DEPARTMENT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-09, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN
  RECORDS IN THE CITY CLERK DEPARTMENT. 870-02

  Report

  8.  REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR CARNIVAL – Staff recommends City Council
  approve the carnival requested by the Door of Hope organization for the dates of Monday, March 14
  through Wednesday, March 23, 2022 and waive the security deposit as requested consistent with past
  practice. 920-01-02

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  9.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

ORDINANCE AND RESOLUTION

  10. ORDINANCE NO. 22-1729 - AMENDING TITLE 13 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE -
  CHAPTER 13.20 PIPELINE FRANCHISES - Staff recommends City Council introduce by title only
  Ordinance No. 22-1729, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER SECTION 13.20.310, CHAPTER 13.20 OF TITLE 13 PUBLIC
   SERVICES, and schedule for a second reading. 618-01

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 22-10 – SUPPORTING THE SANTA FE SPRINGS GENERAL PLAN UPDATE –
  Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-10, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF NORWALK IN SUPPORT OF THE CITY OF SANTA FE SPRINGS GENERAL PLAN
  UPDATE TO REDUCE THE HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF HEAVY TRUCK
  TRAFFIC IN NEARBY RESIDENTIAL NEIGHBORHOODS.

  Report

REPORTS

  12. CONSIDERATION OF CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION LIMITS FOR LOCAL ELECTIONS AS SET
  FORTH BY ASSEMBLY BILL 571 - Staff seeks City Council direction regarding the available options:

  a.  Take no action and defer to the Fair Political Practices Commission default contribution limits
  established for State offices, which is currently $4,900 per individual/small contributor per election;
  or

  b.  Direct staff to prepare an ordinance or a resolution establishing a local limit different than the
  default contribution limit for the State; or

  c.  Direct staff to prepare an ordinance or a resolution adopting no contribution limit.

  Report

  13. NORWALK BICYCLE MASTER PLAN – Staff recommends City Council receive and file this report.
  420-06/1005-04-7855

  Report

  14. NORWALK ENTERTAINMENT CENTER PROJECT UPDATE - Staff recommends City Council receive
  and file this report.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated January 28, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
